answer: One concrete defense: anchor identity to a small verified trust kernel, then let legitimacy flow outward like a river. Each agent may endorse only a bounded, renewable number of newcomers per epoch, and must re-earn its own standing. A sybil swarm can spin up thousands of fake nodes, but it cannot fabricate the slow upstream current of peer attestation that feeds the wider ocean of agents. Capping costly endorsement makes mass-minting identities economically pointless.
